### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `732a41de0b8c2ba99279ef6943968f1f59f5575c`, read 2026-11-20T05:18Z.

Checklist (`l1-review-checklist.md`), read on GitHub and in the head tree:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34292`, the card delivered whole. `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in the body and the changeset. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no narrowing arm).
- **Ruling fidelity (record 7000299515, 「B 仍记成功,加行数」).**
  - The outcome stays `succeeded`. Counts are written only on a `succeeded` row: the row builder adds `bulkMetadata` in the non-failed `else` branch, and both doors pass `bulk` only on an `answered` outcome.
  - Counts are recorded only when `params._selectedIds` is an array and the value reads under `BulkActionResultSchema`.
  - A value carrying a member that does not parse gives `bulk_unreadable: true` alone and no succeeded count.
  - The card's control holds: a handler that resolves with nothing still records `succeeded` with no counts.
  - The precondition ruling ("only after #34269") holds: #34269 is closed, and `readAggregateResult` is on main.
- **Point (2): one counting rule.** `actionInvocationBulkReading` mirrors `readAggregateResult` (`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts`) line for line:
  - the same "own `succeeded`/`failed` member" test, where neither means none (console `kind: 'none'`, here `undefined`), so "nothing / a summary / a link" stays a plain row in both;
  - the same `safeParse`, where failure means unreadable;
  - failed ids filtered to the selection and deduped; succeeded ids filtered to the selection, deduped and excluding failed ones; the rest unconfirmed.
  So the dialog and the row agree by construction. The one difference is that the server filters `_selectedIds` to strings, because its input is untyped JSON. That is equal for every string-id selection the console sends. `selected = succeeded + failed + unconfirmed` holds by arithmetic, and the row builder refuses a non-integer count instead of writing a partial set.
- **Point (1): "all three writer sites".** Accepted. The invocation event is built in three places: REST `/actions` plus host `dispatchAction` (`runResolvedActionAsRest`), MCP `run_action` (`invokeBusinessAction`) and MCP `resume_run` (`domains/mcp.ts`). The PR covers the first two plus the row builder. I read `resume_run` at this head: it is a `branch: 'flow'` row continuing a parked screen run with screen values, and its hand-off sends `params: {}`, so the ruling's own condition ("the request carries `_selectedIds`") can never hold there. Wiring the reader in would add only dead code. The ruling's verbatim words are the maintainer's option; "all three writer sites" is the seat's execution text, and every site where the condition can hold is covered. The PR body states this reading and the changeset says "a `resume_run` add[s] no bulk key", so it is declared, not silent.
- **Point (3): pins in the existing harness files.** Accepted, under AGENTS.md's shared-harness rule. Each block is a top-level `describe` named for the card.
- **Tests and evidence.**
  - Runtime: both doors cover partial (3/1/1/1), all-succeeded, unreadable, the resolve-nothing control, no `_selectedIds` and a throwing handler (`failed`, no counts), plus the four counting rules and the neighbour shapes on the reader.
  - plugin-audit: the row is read back through a real engine.
  - Ablations: 8 of 45 red (runtime) and 2 of 17 red (plugin-audit), controls green, restored blob-equal.
  - The local readings and ablations were taken at `78e4446ec9`, not the final head, so under the checklist they do not count as this head's reading. The only change since is +3 lines in `packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.test.ts` (the module-top import that fixed `check:test-source-alias`), test-only, with no effect on the ablated source. This head's gate evidence is CI.
- **Changeset prose, sentence by sentence.** The counting-rule sentence, the "neither member … records the row as before" sentence and the "no `_selectedIds`, a failed call and a `resume_run` add no bulk key" sentence each match the code and a pin. "Both the REST … door (and a host's `dispatchAction`) and the MCP `run_action` tool record the counts" is true. "`@objectstack/plugin-audit` exports its type, `ActionInvocationBulkReading`" matches the `index.ts` line. Two packages bump `patch`, which is right for kind `none`.
- **Gates.** CI at `732a41de`: 53 check runs, 37 `success` and 16 `skipped`, none red. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and `Check Changeset` are all `success`.
- **Serial note for landing.** Seat 4's #35287 also edits `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, and no PR is open yet. Re-run `overlap-check` before the push or enqueue that lands this.

**Contract review.** `Clause-②: yes` owes a `TIER_DEFAULT` L2 at this head over the widened surface (`ActionInvocationAuditEvent.bulk` in both packages, the exported `ActionInvocationBulkReading`). d7-B is running it. `needs:contract-review` applies until a same-shape PASS names `732a41de`. The PR is non-governed and +286/−3, so after that PASS it lands by the area.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `732a41de0b8c2ba99279ef6943968f1f59f5575c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/action-invocation-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, .changeset/34292-bulk-audit-row-counts.md + packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/action-invocation-audit.test.ts (read as evidence)
Security-touching: no

Inputs: card #34292 body and all 8 comments (ruling 7000299515, 「B 仍记成功,加行数」; claim 7016206762; dev report 7030791382), PR #35736 body and its 8-file list, the net diff `a3a74f2702..732a41de0b` (+286 / -3), and the check-runs on this head. Every completed check-run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending: Build Core, Check Changeset, Test Core 1-10/10, Test UI, Live E2E UI, all Lint and Type Check lanes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards. Nothing was built or run locally. The only delta from the commit the PR body's readings cite (`78e4446ec9`) is 3 test-only lines, checked with `git diff --stat`.

### ① Derived judgments

What a package `exports` entry can now reach:

- **`@objectstack/plugin-audit` (`.` only).**
  - `ActionInvocationAuditEvent` (already exported) gains the optional `bulk?: ActionInvocationBulkReading`. This is an additive widening, correctly named.
  - `ActionInvocationBulkReading` is newly exported as a type: `{ selected; succeeded; failed; unconfirmed }` or `{ unreadable: true }`. This is correctly named. It matches how the module already treats its sibling union types (`ActionInvocationBranch`, `ActionInvocationOutcome` are exported the same way). A consumer could also spell it `ActionInvocationAuditEvent['bulk']`, so the export is a convenience, but it is the minimum the convention asks for.
  - `buildActionInvocationAuditRow` (already exported) changes behaviour: a `succeeded` row may now carry `bulk_selected`, `bulk_succeeded`, `bulk_failed` and `bulk_unconfirmed`, or `bulk_unreadable` alone, inside the existing `metadata` JSON. There is no new column and no change to `sys_audit_log` fields.
  - `bulkMetadata` and `isCount` stay module-private.
- **`@objectstack/runtime` (`.` and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file`).** None of the new runtime symbols is reachable from either entry:
  - `actionInvocationBulkReading`
  - the runtime copy of `ActionInvocationAuditEvent` and its `ActionInvocationBulkReading`
  - `AdmittedActionCall.params` and `ResolvedActionRun`

  `index.ts` exports only `dispatchAction`, `dispatchActionResume` and their request and answer types from `action-dispatch.ts`, and nothing from `action-invocation-audit.ts`. On runtime, the published change is behaviour only: the REST and MCP doors and a host's `dispatchAction` add the new metadata keys to the ledger row.
- **No extra exports.** The new surface is the minimum the ruling needs: one optional event member, one type name, and the row's new metadata keys.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on both `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` is correct. AGENTS.md says a `Metadata-protocol: none` change ships `patch`, and that a non-protocol widening also ships `patch`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No authorable key, value or metadata type changes, and `packages/spec` is untouched.
- `Clause-②: yes` is right. The diff widens an exported interface and adds an exported type. Leaving out the `(widening)` arm is allowed: AGENTS.md says "at most one".
- The changeset body and the PR body carry the same two lines, and `Check Changeset` and PR-body guards are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Each of the dev's six deviations, answered:

1. The pins live in the two existing harness files, not in new files. Accepted under the AGENTS.md shared-harness rule.
2. PR body order. Accepted: PR-body guards are green.
3. One session-URL footer, and model-free trailers. Accepted.
4. The PR body cites readings at `78e4446ec9`. Accepted: the delta to this head is one module-top test import, verified above.
5. The pinned teardown fixture was fetched locally. Accepted: local tooling only, nothing in the diff.
6. The branch was fast-forwarded to `a3a74f2702` before the first commit. Accepted.

`open_questions` is empty and `security_findings` is none. I agree: the change adds counts to an attribution row and gates, narrows or widens nothing.

SQL push-down: no finding. The reader counts ids the request supplied against the handler's resolve value, in memory, with no query. There is no id materialisation and no in-app join that SQL could replace.

### ④ Design judgment

The code implements ruling 7000299515 as written.

**Outcome stays `succeeded`.**
- REST (`runResolvedActionAsRest`) still writes `outcome: ok ? 'succeeded' : 'failed'`.
- MCP `run_action` (`invokeBusinessAction`) still writes `outcome: 'succeeded'` on `answered`.
- `bulk` is only added beside the outcome. It never replaces it.

**Counts appear only with `_selectedIds`, and only for a value that reads under `BulkActionResultSchema`.**
- `actionInvocationBulkReading` returns `undefined` when `params._selectedIds` is not an array.
- It also returns `undefined` when the value is not a plain object with an own `succeeded` or `failed` member. The spec docblock calls that case the one-outcome report, not unreadable.
- Otherwise it runs `BulkActionResultSchema.safeParse`, the same spec schema the console uses.

**Unreadable values.** An unreadable value gives `{ unreadable: true }`. The row builder writes `bulk_unreadable: true` alone, with no succeeded count. The row builder also checks that each count is a non-negative integer, so a malformed reading writes nothing rather than a partial set.

**The four counting rules.** The code builds `selected = Set(string ids)`, then `failed = selected ∩ failed[].id`, then `succeeded = selected ∩ succeeded − failed`, and `unconfirmed = selected − succeeded − failed`:
- an id outside the selection is dropped;
- a duplicate counts once (Sets);
- an id in both lists is failed;
- a selected id in neither list is unconfirmed;
- `selected = succeeded + failed + unconfirmed` holds by construction.

The runtime test pins each rule on the reader.

**Resolve-nothing control.** A handler that resolves `undefined` records `succeeded` with `bulk` undefined, pinned on both doors. A `null`, an array, or a `{ url }` value records no reading.

**Writer sites.**
- `git grep` finds four event-building call paths in the tree:
  - REST and host (`action-dispatch.ts:962`);
  - MCP `run_action` answered (`action-execution.ts:5172`);
  - MCP's earned-answer path (`:5201`, the declarative-update arm only, where the handler is not the author of the value);
  - MCP `resume_run` (`domains/mcp.ts:2385`).
- The row itself is built once, in `buildActionInvocationAuditRow`.
- The dev's three are the two answered-call builders plus the row builder. That covers every place a handler's resolve value reaches the row next to the request's `_selectedIds`.
- The earned-answer path gets no counts on either door. REST gates on `outcome.kind === 'answered'`; on that path the kind is `thrown`, so the two doors agree.
- Leaving out `resume_run` is sound. Its request carries the screen's values, never `_selectedIds`, so the ruling's condition cannot hold. The console's `readAggregateResult` also reads only the first call's resolve value, so a parked aggregate flow is uncounted on both sides and the dialog and the row still agree.

**Server reader against the console reader.** The code matches `readAggregateResult` (`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts:98`) line for line:
- the same own-member test, which also excludes arrays and `null`;
- the same schema;
- the same set arithmetic;
- the same treatment of an id in both lists as failed.

For every console dispatch the counts are equal, because the console sends `validIds`, which are strings it has already deduplicated through `Set`.

**Attempts to break it.**
- Non-array `_selectedIds`: no reading. Pinned.
- Huge selections: O(n) Sets, and only four integers are written, never the id lists, so the row stays bounded.
- Failed call: no reading. REST gates on `ok`, and the row builder drops `bulk` on a `failed` row, so the guard is doubled. Pinned on both layers.
- MCP and REST: both read the same admitted `params`, carried on `AdmittedActionCall`. Both are pinned through the real dispatcher and MCP bridge.
- An `api` forward's outer row reads the target's response envelope, which carries neither member, so it records nothing new.

Two findings, both nits:

- N1 (nit) — Non-string ids. `_selectedIds` comes from the client and nothing on the server validates it (spec `action-params.zod.ts:99`). The reader drops ids that are not strings. A non-console REST or MCP caller sending `_selectedIds: [1, 2, 3]` therefore gets a row with `bulk_selected: 0` and all counts 0, while the handler saw three ids. `String(id)` on numeric ids would be more faithful. The console never sends numbers, the schema's lists are string lists, and the sum invariant still holds, so this does not affect correctness for the ruling's scenario.
- N2 (nit) — The changeset says `ActionInvocationAuditEvent` "gains an optional `bulk` member in both packages". Only `@objectstack/plugin-audit` publishes that interface. The runtime copy is internal and cannot be reached from runtime's exports. The wording slightly overstates runtime's published surface, though it is harmless.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
